name: Tolkcontact
developerCountry: Netherlands (Bilthoven); app built by nWise AB, Uppsala, Sweden
oneLine: Dutch app from the national interpreting service: a sign language interpreter by video, phone calls through KPN Teletolk and 112, paid by health insurance.

platforms.detail: Tolkcontact says the app runs on Android phones and tablets, iPhones and iPads, and Windows computers, laptops and tablets.

deviceRequirements.detail: The Dutch App Store lists iOS 15.0 or later. The app needs Wi-Fi or mobile internet, and Tolkcontact says it has limited support on Xiaomi, BlackBerry and Unihertz phones.

roomCaptions.text: Through interpreters: NGT by video, or a booked schrijftolk
roomCaptions.detail: With Tolk op afstand, a Sign Language of the Netherlands (NGT) interpreter joins by video when you're with a hearing person, in sign language, not text. For live text you book a writing interpreter (schrijftolk) through mijn.tolkcontact.nl, who types everything said onto a tablet, in person or by video. Writing interpreters can't be called on the spot through the app.

groupConversations.text: Schrijftolk writes who says what; video interpreting less suited
groupConversations.detail: A writing interpreter's text shows what is said and by whom. Tolkcontact says remote interpreting suits meetings with many people less well, because the interpreter can't see who is talking.

languages.detail: Interpreters work in Sign Language of the Netherlands (NGT), Sign Supported Dutch (NmG) and spoken Dutch; for another language the interpreter decides. The app is in Dutch only.

offline.text: No, needs Wi-Fi or mobile internet
offline.detail: Every service in the app is a live connection to a person, and Tolkcontact says the app needs Wi-Fi or mobile internet.

speakerLabels.text: A schrijftolk writes who says what
speakerLabels.detail: Writing interpreters write who said each thing. The app itself shows no speaker labels; it connects you to people.

translation.text: NGT and Dutch; other languages if the interpreter agrees
translation.detail: Interpreters translate between sign language and spoken Dutch. For a conversation in another language, the interpreter decides whether they can do it.

saveTranscripts.text: No, sessions may not be recorded
saveTranscripts.detail: Interpreters have a professional code and a duty of confidentiality, and you may not record a Tolk op afstand session without Tolkcontact's explicit permission.

fileUpload.detail: Not on Tolkcontact's pages for deaf users.

display.text: Text size (5 steps) and colours in text calls
display.detail: In text calls you set your own and the interpreter's text size (extra small to extra large) and text and background colours.

soundAlerts.text: A schrijftolk describes sounds in the text
soundAlerts.detail: Writing interpreters type what can be heard around you, such as a phone beeping or someone sneezing. Tolkcontact's pages mention no sound alerts in the app.

phoneCalls.text: Yes, KPN Teletolk relay; own 085 number
phoneCalls.detail: Through KPN Teletolk you call and get called in text (24 hours a day) or Sign Language of the Netherlands (7:00 to 22:00), and can also speak yourself; an operator voices what you type or sign and turns the reply into text or sign language. You get a personal 085 number. 112 can be called by voice or text, answered in text.

videoCalls.text: Video calls with app users; relay in sign language
videoCalls.detail: You can video call other people who have the app, and KPN Teletolk relays calls in sign language by video.

humanCaptioners.detail: Every service is done by people: KPN Teletolk operators on calls, NGT interpreters by video, and booked writing interpreters who type live text.

signLanguage.detail: Tolk op afstand connects you with a Sign Language of the Netherlands interpreter by video, without an appointment, seven days a week from 7:00 to 22:00, for up to 20 minutes per conversation. Sign language calls through KPN Teletolk run at the same hours.

privacy.text: Human interpreters with a duty of confidentiality
privacy.detail: Interpreters have a professional code and a duty of confidentiality, and sessions are not recorded. The App Store label says the developer collects no data; Tolkcontact's privacy statement lists your BSN for the insurer claim and your live location when you call 112.

account.text: Yes, requested; BSN and proof of deafness
account.detail: You request an account at tolkcontact.nl/app, or activate it with one click if you have mijn.tolkcontact.nl through UWV interpreting hours. The application asks for name, address, date of birth and citizen service number (BSN), and the insurer needs proof of deafness such as an audiogram or a GP's letter.

availability.detail: The app is for deaf and hard of hearing people in the Netherlands, with Dutch interpreters only. Tolk op afstand works anywhere in Europe, Tolkcontact says, and may not work outside it.

freePlan.text: Calls free; app paid by health insurance
freePlan.detail: Calls through KPN Teletolk, to 112 and to Tolkcontact's customer service are free. The app subscription is paid by your health insurer or employer, and remote interpreting uses your interpreting hours.

price.detail: Every Dutch health insurer covers the app for deaf and hard of hearing people, with no eigen risico, most from 35 dB of hearing loss. Through an employer it costs €250 a year excl. VAT (the employer page says €20.66 a month per employee). Without interpreting hours a remote interpreter is billed at 130% of the normal rate; booking through Tolkcontact costs €82 per booking plus €81.61 an hour (excl. VAT, 2026).

accessibilityFunding.text: Insurer pays app; UWV interpreting hours
accessibilityFunding.detail: Health insurers pay for the app. Interpreters are paid from interpreting hours granted by UWV: 30 a year for private situations (168 if deafblind), 15% of working time for employees, and 1,000 a year at school or in higher education (1,600 in MBO), funded by three ministries. In private situations the first 15 hours of remote interpreting cost one hour per three.

strengths.text: A Sign Language of the Netherlands interpreter by video, without an appointment, every day from 7:00 to 22:00, for conversations of up to 20 minutes.
Free phone calls through KPN Teletolk, by text 24 hours a day or in sign language from 7:00 to 22:00, with a personal 085 number for incoming calls.
Paid by public money: health insurers cover the app, and UWV grants interpreting hours (30 a year for private situations).
Direct 112 calls by voice or text, answered in text, with your live location shared.

limits.text: For the Netherlands only, with Dutch interpreters (NGT and Dutch writing interpreters).
Writing interpreters can't be called on the spot through the app; they are booked in advance.
Remote interpreting is for short conversations of at most 20 minutes, from 7:00 to 22:00.
An account needs an application with your BSN and proof of deafness, and the app is in Dutch only.

notes: Tolkcontact is the national interpreter-booking service run by Berengroep (Bilthoven) on behalf of UWV; the app is built by nWise AB (Uppsala, Sweden), the App Store seller. The brief's www.tolkcontact.nl/app redirects to /tolkcontact-app/aanvragen/. Funding: the app is paid by health insurers (zorgverzekering), not by UWV or the gemeente; UWV pays the interpreters through interpreting hours. No page mentions the gemeente or the Wlz for the app or interpreters, so neither is used. Conflicts: (1) Employer price: the app's cost page says €250 a year excl. VAT; the employer page says €20.66 a month per employee (€247.92 a year). The table uses €250. (2) Privacy: the App Store label says 'no data collected', while Berengroep's privacy statement (19 Feb 2025) lists IP or MAC address, contact data, the application form (name, address, date of birth, BSN, email) and live location for 112. KPN Teletolk's own site (teletolk.nl) was not opened; Teletolk facts come from Tolkcontact's pages. Not found: speech-to-text, voice names, speaker direction, export, file upload, summaries, custom words. The app is not in the US App Store (lookup API returned no result), so appStoreUrl is the Dutch store. The App Store and Google Play listings were read but no star ratings are used. All pages opened with curl on 2026-11-02 and read as text.
